findings.reason: a bound the stated mechanism cannot meet either fails a correct node at its gate or pushes the worker to weaken the test, and the fix is one clause: state it against the stored offset (64 plus the bytes from offset to EOF) rather than against bytes appended.
findings.text: the measure "the bytes it reads from each stream per tick are at most the bytes appended plus 64, and zero for a stream that did not grow" omits the unconsumed trailing record: `station_store.ingest_stream` reads to EOF (`handle.read()`, station_store.py:418-419) and advances `consumed` only past whole lines (`_whole_lines`, :181), so a tick that lands mid-record leaves those bytes to be re-read next tick from offset−64, making a correct read 64 + unconsumed tail + appended; the section's own rule ("up to the last whole record") makes a mid-record tick the normal case for fixture streams replayed "in chunks", so the bound fails on the implementation the section specifies

findings.reason: the guarantee is narrower than the claim, so a node can implement and test exactly what §6 says and still serve a stale fold for a stream recreated between ticks, which is the defect the section exists to prevent.
findings.text: §6 calls the tail anchor the catch for "the one case neither an inode nor a size test can see", but the anchor is read only for a stream that grew (so an in-place rewrite that keeps or reduces its size while staying at or above the stored offset is read by nothing) and covers only the bytes in [offset−64, offset) (so a rewrite changing earlier bytes only produces a match and no refold); separately, "a stream ... that shrank" at :163 cannot be evaluated as written because the `streams` table carries path, inode, consumed, fold_state and observation and no previous size, leaving `ingest_stream`'s `stored <= info.st_size` as the only shrink test

findings.reason: a surface or coordinator reading the recommended section from the attribute is sent to a landed section, which is the staleness the earlier rewrite of this followup set out to remove and left half-done.
